## Who the user is

Imam Taufiq (also seen as Imam Digmi online). Based in the Bogor area, Indonesia, holds an S.Kom. Main language is Bahasa Indonesia; comfortable in English for technical and professional topics. Mixes Indonesian and English for tech discussions, keeping terms like pipeline, deployment, ingestion and model training in English.

Married, with a child about 13-14 months old in September-October 2026.

Work: Data Engineer at Hassad Food, Qatar, working remotely from Indonesia. The company requires physical presence in its operating country. As of October 2026 the visa and contract status is unconfirmed and still in application.

Study: Master's in Information Technology (MTI) at BINUS University, started September 2025, three-semester system. Thesis proposal passed; preparing the pre-thesis outline. Topic: detecting date palm trees from high-resolution satellite imagery over Qatar, aiming to produce individual tree coordinates.

## Preferences and how to help

- Style: practical, direct, specific. Very short answers for simple factual questions, quizzes and quick translations; long in-depth explanations are welcome for complex technical topics.
- Accuracy: wants technical accuracy and admission of uncertainty over invented answers. Accepts corrections. Asks for evidence, documentation or references.
- Technical help: ready-to-run terminal commands, Python, SQL, step-by-step guides, and real-scenario examples. When something fails, wants the root cause, not just a workaround; often shares error logs.
- Solutions: fit the actual environment, practical, not over-engineered. Prefers simpler options when complexity is not justified. Likes comparing several architectures with trade-offs in performance, cost and complexity, weighing technical and financial factors together, and discussing long-term consequences.
- Formats: ASCII or Mermaid diagrams for pipelines; Markdown for research notes; DOCX when manual editing and tidy layout are needed; plain copy-paste text when no file is needed.
- Learning: cycle of reading concepts, implementing, debugging, comparing alternatives and asking follow-ups.
- Academic writing: structured and logically argued, with clear novelty and scientific references. APA 7th edition. Research should make a real scientific contribution, not just report a company implementation.
- Professional English: concise. CVs as bullet points starting with action verbs.
- Hardware and purchases: values value-for-money and real working needs over top specs. Compares Mac mini, MacBook Air and MacBook Pro, and weighs Singapore purchases against Indonesian prices, including tax and GST refund.

Arabic learning: studying Modern Standard Arabic (Fusha) and Saudi dialect (Amiyyah). Default is Fusha with harakat, unless Amiyyah is requested; sometimes text without harakat is wanted. Wants natural, idiomatic Saudi usage rather than literal translation, and corrections when a phrase is off. Quick-translation prefixes: `in:` for Indonesian to Arabic, `ar:` for Arabic to Indonesian, with no long explanations in that mode. Exercises with many sentences use a side-by-side table of Arabic and Indonesian.

## Important people

Work colleagues:
- Saad: main stakeholder and frequent coordination partner.
- Ahmed: internal project work.
- Tahir: CRM development.
- Essam: data support for Dandy.
- Samer: VM and database work for the Ministry.
- Reza: visa matters.

Academic: Prof. Dr. Sani Muhamad Isa, S.Si., M.Kom., target thesis supervisor.

Family: spouse, child (13-14 months as of Sep-Oct 2026), and the user's mother. The mother travelled to Makkah and was scheduled to return in September 2026. When planning family trips, the user considers the young child's comfort and extra time needed.

Religious study: Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A., ustadz who leads book study for the Makkah & Madinah Mengaji group (about 5-7 members) at Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (Nustro). The group meets on Wednesdays after Maghrib, every two weeks, until about 20:00-21:00. The user also asks for help writing Arabic messages to the ustadz and study partners.

Data partners: the user handles or monitors integration from Carrefour Qatar, Dandy, Al-Meera, Lulu Hypermarket, Rawabi (G1, G2, Warehouse sources), Abu Khalifa and Ansar Gallery. The Ministry of Municipality, Qatar is the government stakeholder for the national food security data integration project. The Ministry requests CSV or Excel and has rejected JSON.

## Platforms and tools

Messaging: Telegram is the chosen main channel for agent notifications. A WhatsApp integration with Hermes has been explored; the user asked whether it needs a new phone number or SIM.

Personal AI: building Hermes Agent as a long-term assistant for work and study. Hindsight is the local memory engine (Web UI on port 9999) with a memory bank named hermes. Goal: a more autonomous research assistant with a critic or reviewer agent, storing findings in a reviewable Obsidian vault on GitHub. Research sources: journals, papers and GitHub; also YouTube and Medium for learning.

Devices: macOS is the main OS. A Windows VM for GIS work is accessed through Windows App; some internal resources are reachable only from the office VM. The MacBook Pro suffered a logic board failure that caused data loss, including part of the thesis dataset and previous Hermes sessions. The repaired MacBook is confirmed back in normal use. The user also has an ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 2024 with an NVIDIA RTX 4050.

Data stack: Azure as main cloud, Azure Data Factory for orchestration, Blob Storage as landing zone, SQL Server as Operational Data Store, Azure SQL, with Python, SQL, PowerShell and ETL/ELT work. Frontend: SvelteKit, MapLibre GL JS, Tailwind CSS.

Geospatial and AI: ArcGIS Pro, QGIS, CVAT, YOLO, DeepLabV3. Experience with NVIDIA GPUs and Apple Silicon.

Home lab: considering a Mac mini as an always-on AI server and home lab, a MacBook Air as a portable work machine, and a VPS. Wants AI infrastructure that runs independently and is continuously available.

## Current goals and commitments

Thesis: about six months available as of February 2026; preparing the outline. Target: a strong contribution with clear novelty and publication in a Q1 or Q2 international journal. Side paper candidate TICO-OBB, not yet confirmed as the thesis topic.

PhD: plans to pursue a PhD in Saudi Arabia, KAUST first choice, with a King Abdulaziz University scholarship also explored. Fields: data science, data engineering, computer vision, AI and remote sensing. Building a research portfolio to support the application.

Active high-priority projects: Qatar Food Security, Digital Twin (map-based SvelteKit and MapLibre app), and the thesis.

Upcoming: collect the repaired MacBook from a friend returning to Indonesia around 8 November 2026.

Past event: a Singapore trip planned for 7 October 2026 has passed; treat as historical.

Open items: Ansar Gallery / Agrico data integration was delayed and needs rescheduling. Visa and contract status for October 2026 is unresolved.

## Interests beyond work

Islamic studies: Riyadhus Shalihin, Al-Ushul As-Sittah by Syaikh Muhammad bin Abdul Wahhab, and Ushul As-Sunnah by Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal, within a study circle led by an ustadz. Common phrases: 'Insyaa Allah' and 'Barakallahu fiikum'.

Creative project: Siyar, 'The Living Atlas of Islamic Scholarship', inspired by Siyar A'lam An-Nubala. Primary creative project.

Fitness: home equipment includes a barbell, two 10 kg plates, two 3 kg dumbbells, resistance bands, a bench and a kettlebell.

Gaming: PlayStation 1 and 2 games and emulation.

## Uncertainties in the record

- Whether the Hermes WhatsApp integration was set up is not recorded; only the SIM/phone number question appears. Telegram is the stated main channel.
- The visa, contract and work-policy situation for October 2026 is not confirmed.
- Whether the mother has returned from Makkah is not recorded; only a planned September 2026 return is known.
- Some items are inferred rather than stated, including a preference for local-first AI infrastructure, which is unconfirmed.

The user's mother returned from Makkah in September 2026. Family flu cases in September included a child who tested positive for Influenza A. None are active tasks.
- **Device budget (historical):** About USD 2,180 was once saved for a replacement device, with spending around USD 2,000 intended. This is not the current financial position. The user has compared Apple prices in Indonesia and Singapore, Apple Trade-In, and Singapore GST refund rules.

## Overview

The memory bank has no curated routine summary yet (the 'Active Tasks & Commitments' and 'User Profile' models are empty and stale). This answer is built from raw observations and facts. It does not record a daily wake-up time, a daily check-in time, or a fixed work-hours schedule. Where a fact is labelled as past or planned, that status is kept below.

## Daily routines

- Daily data delivery (work): operational data is usually delivered every day using T-1 data, meaning the previous day's transactions (recorded in the memory bank without a date).
- Daily ingestion for new sources: Gulf Food was asked for monthly historical data from January 2024, with daily ingestion planned to start in August 2026. Abu Khalifa was planned to provide fresh products through an API from August 2026, with historical data since 2024 and daily ingestion.
- Daily study-related work: no fixed daily study slot is recorded.

## Weekly routines and recurring events

- Weekly data schedule (work): Agrico previously used a weekly data schedule every Thursday (recorded as a past arrangement). The Ansar Gallery integration was delayed and needs to be rescheduled as a follow-up.
- Weekly group study (religious): the user planned a kajian (study session) with the group Makkah & Madinah Mengaji every Wednesday after Maghrib, once every two weeks, until about 20:00–21:00. The location is Masjid As Sakinah Nusantara (also called Nustro). The group has about 5–7 members and studies kitab with ustadz Abdul Wahhab, Lc., M.A. Recorded as planned, so the current status is not confirmed.
- Study-program rhythm: the Master of Information Technology (MTI) at BINUS University runs on a three-semester system with two periods per semester. The user started in September 2025.

## Dated commitments and deadlines

- Thesis: in February 2026 the user said about six months were available for thesis work. By 2026 the user had passed the thesis proposal stage and was preparing the outline/pre-thesis.
- MacBook pickup: the user planned to collect a repaired MacBook from a friend who is returning to Indonesia around 8 November 2026.
- Past items, not upcoming: a Changi Airport trip on 7 October 2026 at 15:30 (with a Jewel Changi visit 30–60 minutes before the flight), and a mother's trip to Makkah scheduled to return in September 2026. These are before the current date (16 October 2026).

## Schedule constraints

- Work location: the user works remotely from Indonesia as a Data Engineer at Hassad Food, Qatar. The company requires physical presence in the country where it operates, which is a constraint on this arrangement.
- Visa and employment status: as of October 2026 the visa, contract, and work-policy status could not be confirmed, and the visa application was still in progress.
- Family: the user is married and has a child about 13–14 months old (September–October 2026). When planning family travel, the user considers the young child's comfort and needs extra time.
- Priority projects: Qatar Food Security, the Digital Twin application, and the thesis are the active high-priority projects, with remote sensing research as the focus.
- Hardware and budget: the user values value-for-money and considered a budget of about USD 2,000 for a replacement device (a historical figure, not a current one).

## Check-in and reminder preferences

- Channel: the user chose Telegram as the main channel for agent notifications. WhatsApp integration was explored, with a question about whether it needs a new phone number or SIM, but Telegram is the chosen primary channel.
- Reminder timing: no explicit preferred reminder time or frequency is recorded.
- Response style for reminders and check-ins: direct, practical, and specific communication. Keep simple factual or quick answers very short. Give longer, in-depth explanations only for complex technical topics.
- Format: plain text that is easy to copy-paste is often enough. Use DOCX only for documents that need manual editing.
- Honesty: the user prefers the assistant to admit uncertainty rather than invent information, and wants inconsistencies corrected.
- Religious and personal context: the user often uses phrases such as 'Insyaa Allah' and 'Barakallahu fiikum'. Reminders for the Wednesday study group should respect this schedule.
